name: Metolazone

overview.mechanism: Inhibits renal tubular sodium reabsorption, predominantly at the cortical diluting site.
uses: Edema, including edema associated with heart failure; hypertension (Philippine Metoz insert) [[PHPI]].
Cardiac or renal edema, including nephrotic syndrome; hypertension (US label) [[USPI]].
overview.uses_note: Philippine product: Metoz 5 mg tablet, made by Centaur Pharmaceuticals (India) and imported and distributed by DéGa International Pharma Corp., listed on the FDA Philippines verification portal as DR-XY43102 (Alu/Alu blister of 10s, box of 30) [[PHFDA]]. Uses and doses here follow its package insert [[PHPI]]; the US label is shown for comparison.

usual_adult_dose.dose: 5–10 mg orally once daily; in some cases 20 mg or more may be required. No more than 80 mg in any 24-hour period [[PHPI]]
Has been used with furosemide or another loop diuretic; monitor electrolytes closely [[PHPI]]
2.5–5 mg daily, alone or with another antihypertensive; an initial 1.25 mg has also been used. Adjust after 3–4 weeks by response; a maintenance dose of 5 mg on alternate days may be used [[PHPI]]
5–20 mg orally once daily; individualize and titrate to minimum effective maintenance dose [[USPI]]

contraindications: Anuria; hepatic coma or precoma; known allergy or hypersensitivity to metolazone [[USPI,PHPI]]

serious: Severe hyponatremia/hypokalemia, volume depletion, arrhythmias, hypersensitivity and severe skin reactions [[USPI]]
Rapid-onset hyponatremia and/or hypokalemia: stop the drug and start supportive measures when symptoms appear [[PHPI]]

monitoring: Electrolytes, renal function, blood pressure and clinical volume/electrolyte status [[USPI,PHPI]]
Blood glucose in patients with diabetes or latent diabetes, and serum uric acid (gout may be precipitated) [[PHPI]]

key_interactions.effect: Increased risk of hypokalemia; salt and water retention (PH insert)
key_interactions.action: Monitor potassium and fluid status (PH insert)
Dose adjustment of the other antihypertensive may be needed (PH insert)

key_interactions.effect: Hypotensive effect may be potentiated by volume contraction (PH insert)

evidence.title: Clinical evidence and prescribing limits
evidence.intro: Package-insert guidance and research evidence are distinguished below. Doses come from the Philippine Metoz insert and the US label, not from these studies.

rows.design: 60 hospitalized adults with loop-resistant acute heart failure; 48-hour comparison.
rows.intervention: Metolazone, IV chlorothiazide or tolvaptan added to IV loop diuretics.
rows.findings: The 3T trial randomized 60 hospitalized patients with acute heart failure and resistance to high-dose IV loop diuretics to oral metolazone, IV chlorothiazide or tolvaptan, alongside IV loop therapy. At 48 hours, weight loss was 4.6 ± 2.7 kg with metolazone, 5.8 ± 2.7 kg with chlorothiazide and 4.1 ± 3.3 kg with tolvaptan; neither comparison against metolazone was statistically significant. [[THREET]]
rows.limitations: Excluded eGFR <15 mL/min/1.73 m² and patients requiring renal replacement therapy or ultrafiltration. Short, monitored inpatient study; no long-term equivalence or dialysis-regimen conclusion [[THREET]].

rows.design: 61 patients hospitalized with loop-resistant heart failure.
rows.intervention: Dapagliflozin versus metolazone for three days.
rows.findings: 61 patients hospitalized with loop-resistant heart failure were randomized to dapagliflozin or metolazone for three days. At 96 hours, mean weight loss was 3.0 versus 3.6 kg (difference 0.65 kg; 95% CI −0.12 to 1.41; P=0.11). Metolazone recipients had larger sodium/potassium decreases and urea/creatinine increases, while serious adverse events were similar. This small short-term comparison does not define dialysis dosing or demonstrate a mortality benefit. [[DAPARESIST]]
rows.limitations: Small, short-term comparison; no mortality benefit or dialysis dosing established.

rows.design: 14 nonedematous patients with stable chronic renal failure; CrCl 1.2–12 mL/min.
rows.findings: Urine flow and sodium excretion increased; potassium excretion also rose slightly [[CKD1972]].
rows.limitations: Very small historical study. Its high experimental doses are not current prescribing recommendations and do not establish contemporary safety.

notes: Zaroxolyn-type and Mykrox-type formulations must not be interchanged at equivalent doses [[USPI]]. The Metoz insert's absorption figures match the Zaroxolyn type, but it cites no bioequivalence study against a US product [[PHPI]].

Accumulation may occur in severe renal impairment. Discontinue if azotemia and oliguria worsen. The overdose section states dialysis is unlikely to be effective; it supplies no chronic HD, PD or CRRT regimen. [[USPI]]

dose_note: The first three lines are from the Philippine Metoz insert [[PHPI]]; the US-label lines are for comparison. The insert describes slow, incomplete absorption (about 65% of a dose in healthy subjects, about 40% in cardiac disease), the profile of Zaroxolyn-type tablets; US labeling warns that Zaroxolyn-type and Mykrox-type (rapid-availability) formulations must not be interchanged dose for dose [[USPI]].

renal: The Metoz insert states that, unlike thiazides in general, metolazone is reported to be effective at a glomerular filtration rate below 20 mL/min [[PHPI]].
Accumulation may occur in severe renal impairment. Discontinue if azotemia and oliguria worsen; anuria is a contraindication [[USPI]].
No chronic HD, PD or CRRT regimen is supplied by either source; the US overdose statement that dialysis is unlikely to be effective is not a dialysis dosing recommendation [[USPI]].
pregnancy: Pregnancy Category B in the Metoz insert: reproduction studies in mice, rabbits and rats at up to 50 mg/kg/day showed no fetal harm, but there are no adequate, well-controlled studies in pregnant women; use only if clearly needed [[PHPI]].
breastfeeding: Metolazone appears in breast milk; the insert advises deciding whether to stop nursing or stop the drug, taking into account the importance of the drug to the mother [[PHPI]].
overdose: No specific antidote. The insert advises gastric evacuation with care to prevent aspiration, then supportive care to maintain hydration, electrolyte balance, respiration, and cardiovascular and renal function [[PHPI]].
